note: The self-check evaluation (31 Oct 2026, after the 12-judge panel). Twenty mastery levels, written by hand before any run: ten clean and ten each with ONE planted fault (fault names the kind). Muse Wonder must pass the clean ones and hold the faulty ones (selfcheck_eval.escript). Each level is a title and three lessons of short beats, as the self-check reads them.

base.question: A product costs $100. Its price increases by 50%, then decreases by 50%. What is its final price?
base.diagnosis: takes the second change of the original amount

fractions.question: Work out 1/2 + 1/3.
fractions.diagnosis: adds the tops and the bottoms

density.question: A block has a mass of 200 g and a volume of 50 cm^3. What is its density?

speed.question: A car drives 60 km at 30 km/h, then 60 km at 60 km/h. What is its average speed?
speed.diagnosis: averages the two speeds instead of total distance over total time

negatives.question: Work out -7 + 3.
negatives.diagnosis: adds the sizes and keeps the sign

lessons.title: The shop till after a rise and a cut
beats: Your step: $100 + $50 = $150, then $150 - $50 = $100. Run it at a shop till.
Check: a $100 jacket rises 50% then falls 50%. Options: $100, $75, $50. Right: $75, because the fall is 50% of $150, which is $75.
The till shows $75: the second change came off the new amount.

lessons.title: Why the second change is bigger
beats: 50% of $150 is $75, not $50: the base grew.

lessons.title: Price the boots sale
beats: Task: boots cost $60. Mark them up 20%, then take 20% off for the sale. Work out the sale price: 60 x 1.2 = 72, 72 x 0.8 = 57.60.
Check: what does the till charge? Options: $60, $57.60, $62.40. Right: $57.60.

lessons.title: A salary rise then a cut
beats: Your step on a pay slip: $1,000 up 10% then down 10%.
Check: what is the pay after both? Options: $1,000, $990, $1,010. Right: $990 (1,000 x 1.1 = 1,100; 1,100 x 0.9 = 990).

lessons.title: The base moves
beats: Each percentage is of the amount just before it.
Check: a tank of 500 L loses 20% then gains 20%. Options: 500 L, 480 L, 520 L. Right: 480 L.

lessons.title: Fix the stock order
beats: Task: stock of 400 items drops 25%, then is restocked by 25% of what is left. Work out the new stock: 400 x 0.75 = 300; 300 x 1.25 = 375.
Check: how many items now? Options: 400, 375, 425. Right: 375.

lessons.title: The shop till after a rise and a cut
beats: Check: a $100 jacket rises 50% then falls 50%. Options: $100, $75, $50. Right: $75.
Charging $100 for it loses the shop $25, because the true price is $75.

lessons.title: Why the second change is bigger
beats: Check: $80 up 25% then down 25%. Options: $80, $75, $85. Right: $75.

lessons.title: Price the boots sale
beats: Task: boots cost $60, up 20% then 20% off: 60 x 1.2 = 72, 72 x 0.8 = 57.60.

lessons.title: Ten percent off
beats: A $50 shirt is 10% off: $5 off, so $45.
Check: 10% off $50. Options: $45, $40, $5. Right: $45.

lessons.title: Twenty percent more
beats: A $40 bag is 20% dearer: $48.
Check: 20% more than $40. Options: $48, $60, $42. Right: $48.

lessons.title: Price the sale rack
beats: Task: a $30 cap is 50% off. Work out the price: $15.
Check: Options: $15, $20, $25. Right: $15.

lessons.title: Half a pizza and a third
beats: Your step: 1/2 + 1/3 = 2/5. Put the slices on one plate.
Check: is 2/5 more or less than the 1/2 you started with? Options: more, less, the same. Right: less, so 2/5 cannot be right.

lessons.title: Make the pieces the same size
Mix the paint order
beats: Task: a painter has 1/3 of a tin of white and 1/4 of a tin of blue. How much paint in all? 4/12 + 3/12 = 7/12 of a tin.
Check: Options: 2/7, 7/12, 1/2. Right: 7/12.

lessons.title: Two part-filled jugs
beats: Your step: adding tops and bottoms: 1/2 + 1/3 = 2/5. Pour the jugs together.
Check: two half-full jugs, 1/2 + 1/2. Your way gives 2/4, a half. Is that right? Options: yes, no. Right: no, it is 1 whole jug.

lessons.title: Cut the timber order
beats: Task: a carpenter needs 1/2 m and 1/5 m of board. Total length: 5/10 + 2/10 = 7/10 m.
Check: Options: 2/7 m, 7/10 m, 1/3 m. Right: 7/10 m.

lessons.title: Half a pizza and a third
beats: Check: is 2/5 less than 1/2? Options: yes, no. Right: yes, so it cannot be the sum.

lessons.title: Make the pieces the same size
Half a pizza and a third
beats: Check: is 2/5 less than 1/2? Options: yes, no. Right: yes.

lessons.title: Make the pieces the same size
beats: 1/2 = 3/6 and 1/3 = 2/6, so the sum is 5/6.

lessons.title: Mix the paint order
beats: Task: 1/3 of a tin of white and 1/4 of a tin of blue: 4/12 + 3/12 = 8/12 of a tin.
Check: Options: 2/7, 8/12, 1/2. Right: 8/12.

lessons.title: Weigh the block in the lab
beats: Your step: 50 / 200 = 0.25 g/cm^3. A metal block that light would float on water.
Check: does a 200 g block of 50 cm^3 sink in water (1 g/cm^3)? Options: sinks, floats. Right: sinks, so 0.25 cannot be its density.

lessons.title: Grams in each cubic centimetre
beats: Density is grams per cm^3: 200 g / 50 cm^3 = 4 g/cm^3.
Check: 90 g in 30 cm^3. Options: 0.33, 3, 2700 g/cm^3. Right: 3 g/cm^3.

lessons.title: Check the supplier's metal
beats: Task: a bar of 540 g and 200 cm^3 is sold as aluminium (2.7 g/cm^3). Work out its density: 540 / 200 = 2.7 g/cm^3.
Check: is it aluminium? Options: yes, no. Right: yes.

lessons.title: A box of feathers and a brick
beats: Your step divides volume by mass. A brick then comes out lighter per cm^3 than feathers.
Check: 1000 g brick of 500 cm^3, your way: 0.5. Is a brick less dense than water? Options: yes, no. Right: no.

lessons.title: Mass on top
beats: Density = mass / volume: 1000 / 500 = 2 g/cm^3.
Check: 300 g in 100 cm^3. Options: 3, 0.33, 30000. Right: 3 g/cm^3.

lessons.title: Sort the scrap metal
beats: Task: a 790 g piece of 100 cm^3: steel is 7.9 g/cm^3, copper 8.9. Work it out: 790 / 100 = 7.9.
Check: which metal? Options: steel, copper. Right: steel.

lessons.title: Litres and cubic centimetres
beats: 1 litre is 1000 cm^3.
Check: 2.5 L in cm^3. Options: 25, 250, 2500. Right: 2500.

lessons.title: Cubic metres
beats: Check: 0.002 m^3 in cm^3. Options: 20, 2000, 200. Right: 2000.

lessons.title: Fill the water tank
beats: Task: a tank of 1.2 m^3. How many litres? 1200 L.
Check: Options: 120, 1200, 12000. Right: 1200.

lessons.title: Weigh the block
beats: A block's mass is 200 g; its volume 50 cm^3.
Check: what is its mass? Options: 200 g, 50 g. Right: 200 g.

lessons.title: Measure the volume
beats: Volume by water displaced: the water rose 50 cm^3.
Check: the volume? Options: 50 cm^3, 200 cm^3. Right: 50 cm^3.

lessons.title: Record the metal sample
beats: Task: write the mass and the volume of the sample in the lab book.
Check: which goes in the mass column? Options: 200 g, 50 cm^3. Right: 200 g.

lessons.title: The two-leg drive
beats: Your step: (30 + 60) / 2 = 45 km/h. Time it: 60 km at 30 km/h is 2 h; 60 km at 60 km/h is 1 h.
Check: 120 km in 3 h. Options: 45 km/h, 40 km/h, 50 km/h. Right: 40 km/h.

lessons.title: Why the slow leg counts more
beats: More time is spent going slowly, so the average leans to the slow speed.
Check: 30 km at 10 km/h then 30 km at 30 km/h. Options: 20, 15, 25 km/h. Right: 15 km/h (60 km in 4 h).

lessons.title: Plan the delivery route
beats: Task: a van does 40 km at 40 km/h and 40 km at 80 km/h. Average speed: 80 km / 1.5 h = 53.3 km/h.
Check: Options: 60, 53.3, 50 km/h. Right: 53.3 km/h.

lessons.title: A runner's two laps
beats: Your step averages the speeds. Lap times: 400 m at 4 m/s takes 100 s; 400 m at 8 m/s takes 50 s.
Check: 800 m in 150 s. Options: 6 m/s, 5.33 m/s, 5 m/s. Right: 5.33 m/s.

lessons.title: Time is the weight
beats: Average speed = total distance / total time.
Check: 10 km at 5 km/h then 10 km at 10 km/h. Options: 7.5, 6.67, 8 km/h. Right: 6.67 km/h.

lessons.title: Set the bus timetable
beats: Task: a bus goes 30 km at 60 km/h and 30 km at 30 km/h. Average: 60 km / 1.5 h = 40 km/h.
Check: Options: 45, 40, 35 km/h. Right: 40 km/h.

lessons.title: The two-leg drive
beats: Your step: (30 + 60) / 2 = 45. The times: 2 h and 1 h.
Check: 120 km in 3 h. Options: 45, 40, 50 km/h. Right: 40 km/h.

lessons.title: Why the slow leg counts more
beats: More time at the slow speed.
Check: 30 km at 10 then 30 km at 30. Options: 20, 15, 25. Right: 15 km/h.

lessons.title: A worked example
beats: Example: 50 km at 50 km/h and 50 km at 25 km/h is 100 km in 3 h, 33.3 km/h.
Example: 20 km at 20 and 20 km at 40 is 40 km in 1.5 h, 26.7 km/h.

beats: Your step: (30 + 60) / 2 = 45. Times: 2 h and 1 h.
Check: 120 km in 3 h. Options: 45, 40, 50 km/h. Right: 40 km/h.

lessons.title: Why the slow leg counts more
beats: More time at the slow speed.
Check: 30 km at 10 km/h then 30 km at 30 km/h. Options: 20, 15, 25 km/h. Right: 20 km/h.

lessons.title: Plan the delivery route
beats: Task: 40 km at 40 km/h and 40 km at 80 km/h: 80 km / 1.5 h = 53.3 km/h.
Check: Options: 60, 53.3, 50. Right: 53.3 km/h.

lessons.title: The freezer thermometer
beats: Your step: 7 + 3 = 10, keep the minus: -10. The freezer is at -7 C and warms 3 degrees.
Check: warmer or colder than -7? Your -10 is colder. Options: warmer, colder. Right: warmer, so -10 cannot be right.

lessons.title: Adding a positive moves right
beats: From -7, three steps right: -6, -5, -4.
Check: -5 + 8. Options: -13, 3, -3. Right: 3.

lessons.title: Log the cold-room temperature
beats: Task: the cold room reads -12 C; the heater adds 5 degrees. Log the new reading: -12 + 5 = -7 C.
Check: Options: -17, -7, 7. Right: -7 C.

lessons.title: A bank balance of -$7
beats: Your step adds the sizes and keeps the sign. You owe $7 and pay in $3.
Check: do you owe more or less now? Your -10 says more. Options: more, less. Right: less: you owe $4.

lessons.title: Opposite signs: subtract the sizes
beats: -7 + 3: 7 - 3 = 4, and the bigger size was negative: -4.
Check: -2 + 9. Options: -11, 7, -7. Right: 7.

lessons.title: Reconcile the account
beats: Task: an account is at -$25; a $40 payment arrives. Work out the balance: -25 + 40 = $15.
Check: Options: -$65, $15, -$15. Right: $15.

lessons.title: Adding positives
beats: Check: 5 + 6. Options: 11, 1, 30. Right: 11.

lessons.title: Adding two negatives
beats: Check: -2 + -5. Options: -7, 7, -3. Right: -7.

lessons.title: Total the deliveries
beats: Task: 12 boxes on Monday and 9 on Tuesday: 21 boxes.
Check: Options: 21, 3, 108. Right: 21.

lessons.title: Two negatives make a positive
beats: Check: -2 x -5. Options: 10, -10, -7. Right: 10.

lessons.title: A negative times a positive
beats: Check: -6 x 2. Options: 12, -12, -4. Right: -12.

lessons.title: Scale the losses
beats: Task: a shop loses $3 a day for 5 days: -3 x 5 = -$15.
Check: Options: -$15, $15, -$8. Right: -$15.
